title: Partner-managed listing integration playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for partner-managed marketplace listings. Focus: reduce friction for partners who want to list their bundles that include Redwood-hosted or partner-hosted components. This is intentionally pragmatic — checklists, minimal tech requirements, example copy snippets, and a lightweight acceptance flow for GTM and security sign-off.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Partner can manage listing content (creative + copy) but must meet our technical and compliance gates.
- Provide a small integration shim (webhook + health endpoint) for telemetry and billing handshake.
- GTM: co-marketing asset requirements + 48-hour pre-publication review window.

Who this doc is for:
- Solutions engineers onboarding partner listings
- Partner success / alliances reps coordinating assets
- Marketplace ops reviewer (legal/compliance)
- Partner engineers building the integration

Assumptions and scope:
- Applies to cloud marketplace listings where partner controls the listing content but Redwood is a required runtime or managed integration.
- Not covering fully private deployments or on-prem packaged ISVs (separate runbook).

Roles and responsibilities (high-level):
- Partner: provide copy, logos, screenshots, technical endpoint, SLA summary, support contact, and test account.
- Redwood SE: validate integration, run quick smoke tests, confirm telemetry and billing handshake.
- GTM: approve co-marketing assets and listing dates.
- Security/Compliance: validate data flows and that no PII leaves partner environment without consent.

Minimum technical checklist (partner-managed variant):
- Health endpoint: /health responding 200 within 500ms for simple auth/no-auth tests.
- Integration webhook: partner must accept POST callback for subscription events (JSON schema below).
- Auth: OAuth2 client credentials or API key depending on partner capability. If API key, keys must be short-lived or rotated per our guidance.
- Telemetry: lightweight usage ping once per day with anonymized counter—samples only for cost attribution.
- Test account: partner provides sandbox credentials with 3 example invocations.
- Rate-limiting expectations documented: e.g., 200 rps sustained, bursting to 1k for 30s.
- Fallback: define behavior if endpoint returns 5xx (our Marketplace should show degraded state and not charge for failed invocations).

Security / compliance quick gates:
- Data classification: partner indicates data types (PII, PHI, business confidential).
- Encryption in transit mandatory (TLS 1.2+).
- No customer secrets logged by partner telemetry (declare where logs are stored).
- If partner handles user data that we store in metadata, ensure retention policy and deletion API.
- Runbook: short checklist for SRE/security to verify (sec team script link in linked_artifacts).

Listing content requirements (creative + copy):
- One-line short description (<= 140 chars) — use imperative and value-first language. Example: "Real-time document summarization powered by Redwood Inference".
- Long description (<= 1000 chars) — who it’s for, core benefits, 2 bullets on how it works, 1 bullet on pricing model.
- 3–6 feature bullets (30–80 chars each). Avoid vendor-speak.
- 2 screenshots: 16:9 PNG, max 2MB each, annotated with captions.
- 1 logo (SVG preferred) + 1 square icon (512x512 PNG).
- Support contact: partner support email + expected SLA hours.
- Compliance statements: e.g., SOC2 status, GDPR controller/processor note if applicable.

Acceptance criteria (what SE/Marketplace ops must check before approving):
- Tech: health check passes, example invocations return expected shape, rate-limits documented, webhook working.
- Copy: short + long descriptions present and pass marketing quick-edit (no passive voice, no superlatives without backup).
- Creative: images present, alt text provided, logos are current.
- Legal: partner agreed to Marketplace terms (link) and provided required indemnities.
- Security: checklist items signed off by security contact or tagged with low-risk exception.

GTM and co-marketing: timeline + checklist
- Assets due: 14 days before proposed publish date.
- Review window: 48–72 business hours for our GTM team to review creative + copy.
- Launch announcement: if Redwood co-markets, partner provides 1 co-branded social post, 1 case study outline, and 2 quote options.
- Metrics to track for 30 days post-launch: conversion rate from listing -> trial, avg usage per trial, support tickets created.

Example listing copy snippets (templates to copy into partner doc):
- Short: "Add configurable LLM inference for in-app experiences — built for predictable latency and cost."
- Medium (3-sentence blurb): "[Partner] + Redwood Inference deliver a managed inference integration that reduces per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs. Quick to configure, easy to monitor, and pre-integrated with Redwood’s billing and observability. Ideal for product teams shipping high-throughput features."
- Feature bullets: "Predictable per-token billing", "KV caching to reduce repeated context cost", "Auto-fallback to regional model pools"

Lightweight integration webhook JSON schema (example):
- event: string (subscription.created | subscription.updated | subscription.cancelled)
- customer_id: string (marketplace id)
- plan_id: string
- timestamp: iso8601
- signature: HMAC-SHA256 header (we verify with shared secret)

Operational run notes (notes to self style):
- SE to run a small smoke harness: 3 sequential calls, 1 parallel burst of 50, webhook receipt confirmed in partner sandbox.
- If webhook fails, mark listing PREVIEW until resolved.
- Document which Redwood model variant the partner expects us to route to (e.g., redwood-open-7b-q8).

Unresolved questions / decisions required:
- Do we require mandatory rotation of partner webhook secrets or allow 90-day rotation? (Security wants 30d, partners hate it).
- Billing handshake: do we require partner to submit usage only or allow Redwood to charge on their behalf? Need legal input.
- Should we mandate a minimum SLA for partner-managed listings to be eligible for co-marketing? (Proposed: 99.5% monthly)

Publisher acceptance workflow (proposal):
1) Partner submits assets + sandbox link to partner-portal (form).
2) Automated smoke tests triggered (health + example calls).
3) SE review with checkboxes (tech + creative + legal).
4) Security quick-scan (within 48h).
5) GTM scheduling and publish date confirmed.

Launch day checklist (day-of):
- Confirm listing live in all target regions.
- Verify telemetry flows from partner to our billing pipeline for first 24h.
- Quick sampling of first 10 trials to ensure expected behavior.
- GTM social posts queued.

Appendix: quick editorial tips for partners (short list):
- Lead with customer problem, not feature.
- Avoid marketing adjectives without proof. Use numbers where possible.
- Keep short description active-voice and benefit-focused.

TODO (this doc):
- [ ] Decide on webhook rotation cadence (action: security).
- [ ] Add sample Postman collection for smoke tests (action: SE team).
- [ ] Draft legal addendum for charge-on-behalf partners (action: legal).
- [ ] Create a one-pager for partners describing GTM co-marketing tiers (action: GTM).

Notes / scratch area (raw):
- Partner wants their own SSO to connect to marketplace console for metrics — possible but needs RBAC scoping.
- Could we allow an ‘embed’ flow for partner UIs where Redwood surfaces embeddable checkout? Follow-up with product.
- If partner includes heavy-weight models (100B+), route to Dedicated pool and require traffic shaping.

End of doc — pinged Gabriel and Sofia for review of tech checklist.
